description: Composite of five TEM bright-field images of the 28Mn0Ni low-density steel after interrupted tensile deformation; all panels carry a 200 nm scale bar. Header text "28Mn0Ni" spans the top with a double-headed arrow. (a) is a vertical panel annotated "HR+CR+973 K" and "ε~0.14", showing a dark tangled dislocation substructure with cell formation and a strongly diffracting band running diagonally. (b)–(e) are the HR+CR+1173 K condition at increasing true strain: (b) ε~0.02 shows widely spaced, faint planar slip traces in an otherwise clean austenite grain; (c) ε~0.08 shows a denser set of long straight slip bands crossing at a second weak orientation; (d) ε~0.30 shows a heavily refined, closely spaced slip-band network with locally wavy/intersecting bands; (e) shows thick dark bands separated by lighter matrix, with two white arrows labelling "Annealing twins", indicating dislocation–twin interaction. Together the panels demonstrate the strain-sequence argument: the partially recrystallized 973 K condition deforms by dislocation multiplication and cross slip into cells (a), whereas the fully recrystallized 1173 K condition evolves from sparse planar slip (b) through slip-band refinement (c,d) to dislocation interaction with prior annealing twins (e). No numeric values are printed on any panel except the stated strain values and scale bars.

observations.observation: The figure is a set of five TEM bright-field micrographs of the 28Mn0Ni alloy after tensile deformation; every panel carries a 200 nm scale bar.
Panel (a) is labelled HR+CR+973 K with a true strain of ε~0.14, whereas panels (b)-(e) belong to the HR+CR+1173 K condition at ε~0.02, 0.08, 0.30 and an unlabelled strain.
The caption states that (a) shows dislocation multiplication and cell formation.
The caption states that (b)-(d) show refinement of slip bands with progress of deformation (strain).
The caption states that (e) indicates interaction between dislocation and prior annealing twins.
Panel (e) carries printed arrows pointing at dark bands labelled 'Annealing twins'.
The citing text reports that dislocations were cutting through fine κ-carbides evolving into slip band structure with a mean slip band spacing of ~200 ± 30 nm.
The citing text states that fine cross-slip activity forming a dislocation cell structure was seen in the deformed austenite regions of the partially recrystallized HR+CR+973 K sample (Fig. 11a).
The citing text states that dislocation-twin interaction shown in Fig. 11e was the dominant strain hardening mechanism in recrystallized alloys.
Slip band spacing visibly decreases from (b) through (d), with the band structure becoming denser and more refined as strain increases.

subfigures.description: TEM bright-field image of 28Mn0Ni in the HR+CR+973 K condition deformed to ε~0.14; dense tangled dislocations with cell formation and a dark diagonal band; 200 nm scale bar.
TEM bright-field image of 28Mn0Ni HR+CR+1173 K deformed to ε~0.02; sparse, faint planar slip traces in a relatively clean recrystallized austenite grain; 200 nm scale bar.

TEM bright-field image at ε~0.30; heavily refined, closely spaced slip band network with locally wavy/intersecting bands; 200 nm scale bar.
